judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the claim about GW250114 being credited with a first direct measurement of the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect. No mention of LIGOScientific:2025rid or any challenge to that specific mis-attributed claim appears in the report.

The review does not mention the LIGOScientific:2025rid citation, GW250114 ringdown paper, or any misattribution about a first direct measurement of nonlinear gravitational-wave memory. There is no source-specific citation challenge matching this injected claim.

The reviewer mentions GW250114 in the summary but fails to notice or challenge the claim that the cited paper (LIGOScientific:2025rid) reports a measurement of the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect.

The reviewer never challenges the claim that GW250114 delivered the 'first direct measurement of the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect' or questions whether reference [5] (LIGOScientific:2025rid) actually supports that claim. The reviewer's comments on GW250114 and the introduction do not flag any topic mis-attribution between the cited paper and the memory-effect claim.
The reviewer consistently references '~200×' speedup throughout the report and does not flag any discrepancy between the abstract's '~201-fold' and the body's '~200 times' figures.

The reviewer repeatedly refers to an approximately 200× speedup, but does not flag any inconsistency between the abstract and body or mention the altered 201-fold value. Mere repetition of the unflagged headline result is not a detection.
The reviewer repeatedly cites the 200x speedup figure from the body of the text and does not notice the 201x discrepancy introduced in the abstract.

The reviewer consistently refers to '~200×' or '200× speedup' throughout the report without noting any discrepancy between the abstract's '~201-fold' and the body's '~200 times' figures. There is no flag of the abstract-vs-body mismatch on the speedup factor.
The reviewer does not flag any issue with the normalisation prefactor (2π)^{N/2} in the conditional posterior of B; no comment addresses the exponent in that equation.

Although the review notes 'Notation glitches are present in Eq. (A.1) and surrounding text,' it does not identify the Gaussian conditional-posterior normalization factor or challenge the specific exponent change from (2π)^N to (2π)^{N/2}. This is too vague to count as a specific detection.
While the reviewer mentions 'notation glitches' in Equation (A.1), the injected error is a specific normalization factor in Section B which the reviewer does not identify or mention.

The reviewer does not flag or question the normalisation prefactor (2π)^{N/2} in equation B.7 for the conditional posterior of B. The review mentions notation glitches in Eq. (A.1) as likely PDF extraction artifacts, but makes no comment about the exponent in the Gaussian normalisation constant being incorrect or the distribution failing to integrate to unity.

The reviewer does not flag the parenthetical claim about doubling nlive yielding indistinguishable posteriors as unverified or phantom evidence; the closest comment is about ESS diagnostics but does not specifically challenge the nlive-doubling assertion.

The reviewer discusses sampler settings and asks for diagnostics, but does not flag the specific parenthetical claim that doubling nlive was verified to yield statistically indistinguishable posteriors, nor note that such a test is unsupported elsewhere in the paper.

The reviewer suggests that the authors should provide more diagnostics and sensitivity tests (mentioning nlive in Question 9), but does not flag the specific phantom claim that a 'doubling nlive' test was already performed.

The reviewer never flags the parenthetical claim about doubling nlive yielding indistinguishable posteriors as unverified or unsupported. While the reviewer requests importance-sampling diagnostics and robustness checks, no specific challenge is made to the nlive doubling assertion, and the closest mention in Question 9 asks about default settings rather than challenging the phantom evidence claim.
